Study with usPhD & postgraduate research degrees
Join us at the Research University of the Year
We're looking for aspiring researchers to join our team and work side-by-side with world-renowned academics to help tackle the big issues facing society.
Named Research University of the Year 2027 by the Daily Mail, the University of Strathclyde is a socially progressive, internationally leading technological University. Our leading-edge research and close links with business, industry and public sector organisations make us the University of choice for 1,800 doctoral researchers from over 80 countries.
Join Strathclyde as a doctoral researcher and help solve issues of global impact!

How to apply
There are two main routes to undertaking a research project at Strathclyde - either by applying for an existing project or pursuing your own specific areas of interest.
Current opportunities
Search our current projects. We've got a range of exciting research projects looking for people just like you!
Projects don't always have funding attached to them. If this is the case, find out ways to fund your research.
If there are no suitable projects, don't worry, you can still apply and submit your own research proposal or topic.
Explore our current opportunities
Submit your own research proposal or topic
You can apply at any time – all you have to do is pick your course and submit your application.

Studying a PhD: your questions answered
Elita, one of our PhD students, explains why she chose to study a PhD and shares info on funding opportunities and other useful advice.
When I spoke to my supervisors at the beginning of my application, they were pretty clear, that they wanted to support me, not just with the admission process, but also the funding and application processes.
Work alongside world-class academics
Imagine being part of a dynamic community of brilliant minds, working alongside world-renowned academics at the forefront of cutting-edge research.
At Strathclyde, we don't just offer a doctoral degree - we offer an opportunity to make a real impact on the world. Our strong links with business, industry, and the public sector mean that our doctoral researchers are tackling some of the most pressing local, societal, and global challenges of our time.
Our state-of-the-art facilities and outstanding research environment offer doctoral researchers the resources and support they need to reach their full potential.

Industry case study: Continuous Manufacturing & Crystallisation
The centre for Continuous Manufacturing & Crystallisation (CMAC), highlights how effectively the University works with industry.
Based in our Technology & Innovation Centre, we're working with companies such as GSK, Pfizer and Astrazeneca to create an effective partnership with industry, academia and public bodies.
Find out more about the centre and how it benefits both our PhD candidates and our industry partners.
We've been able to hire the students that CMAC has trained, directly into our programmes. With the training that they have they're able to make an impact, almost immediately.
Dr Kevin Girrard
Research Fellow at Pfizer

What's the right research degree for you?
There are two types of research degrees:
Doctoral degrees such as PhDs or Professional Doctorates
Masters research degrees including MRes or MPhil
Our guide explores the different types of research degrees to help you decide which is the best fit for you.

PGR Enhancement & Development
The PGR Enhancement and Development programme at the University of Strathclyde provides a comprehensive, student-centred research and training environment designed to support the growth and development of current and future research talent.
The PGR Enhancement and Development Team works closely with all four faculties to enhance the postgraduate research experience, providing opportunities for researcher development and collaboration, and ensuring that training and support provision is of the highest quality.
Throughout your research degree, you’ll have access to a wide range of training, development opportunities, events, and support designed to help you make the most of your postgraduate research experience.
